description: Golden dataset — Q/R de référence annotées manuellement. Chaque ground_truth est vérifiée dans le corpus AWS (PDF officiels). Répartir sur les services et niveaux. Compléter jusqu'à 50 items pour la version finale.

items.question: What is the difference between a security group and a network ACL in AWS?
items.ground_truth: Security groups act at the instance level and are stateful: return traffic is automatically allowed regardless of rules. Network ACLs act at the subnet level and are stateless: return traffic must be explicitly allowed by rules. Security groups support allow rules only, while network ACLs support both allow and deny rules, evaluated in number order.

items.question: What durability does Amazon S3 Standard storage class provide?
items.ground_truth: Amazon S3 Standard is designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) of durability of objects over a given year, by redundantly storing data across multiple devices in a minimum of three Availability Zones.

items.question: How does IAM policy evaluation handle an explicit deny?
items.ground_truth: An explicit deny in any applicable policy overrides any allows. The evaluation logic starts by assuming all requests are implicitly denied, then evaluates all applicable policies; if any policy contains an explicit Deny statement that matches the request, the final decision is deny, regardless of Allow statements elsewhere.

items.question: What happens to data on an instance store volume when the EC2 instance is stopped?
items.ground_truth: Data on instance store volumes is lost when the instance is stopped, hibernated, or terminated, because instance store is ephemeral storage physically attached to the host. Data persists only through an instance reboot.

items.question: What is the maximum execution timeout for an AWS Lambda function?
items.ground_truth: The maximum timeout for a Lambda function is 900 seconds (15 minutes). If the function runs longer, Lambda terminates it.

items.question: What baseline storage performance does Amazon RDS provide on gp3 volumes?
items.ground_truth: On gp3 storage volumes, Amazon RDS provides a baseline storage performance of 3000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s. When the storage size for gp3 volumes reaches a certain threshold, the baseline storage performance increases.

items.question: What does a VPC security group control and at what level does it operate?
items.ground_truth: A VPC security group acts as a virtual firewall that controls inbound and outbound traffic for resources in the VPC. It operates at the resource level. By default a new security group allows all outbound traffic and no inbound traffic until rules are added. Security groups can only be used with resources in the VPC for which they were created.

items.question: In AWS Lambda, what is the difference between reserved concurrency and provisioned concurrency?
items.ground_truth: Reserved concurrency sets the maximum number of simultaneous executions for a function and guarantees that portion of the account concurrency limit to it. Provisioned concurrency pre-initializes a specified number of execution environments so they respond with no cold start latency. Reserved concurrency has no extra cost, while provisioned concurrency is billed for the amount configured.

items.question: What is the difference between SSE-S3 and SSE-KMS server-side encryption in Amazon S3?
items.ground_truth: SSE-S3 uses keys fully managed by Amazon S3 with AES-256. SSE-KMS uses AWS Key Management Service keys, giving separate permissions, an audit trail of key usage, and the ability to create and manage customer managed keys. SSE-KMS offers more control and auditability at the cost of KMS request charges.

items.question: On a gp3 EBS volume, what baseline IOPS and throughput are provided by default?
items.ground_truth: A gp3 EBS volume provides a baseline of 3000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s of throughput by default, independent of volume size. Additional IOPS and throughput can be provisioned separately up to the volume limits.
